1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with good spacing and contrast across all screens, though exact dyslexia-specific font metrics cannot be confirmed from screenshots.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case, no italics or all-caps, and short non-dense blocks of text throughout.

3.why: Layouts are single-column, uncluttered, and clearly sized for mobile screens with readable controls.

4.why: All instructions are brief and plain, e.g. 'Start your security setup.', 'Get a six-digit identity code for this demo.'

5.why: The six-digit code field shows an example placeholder '123456', and the login page shows demo email/password examples.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long block of text; content is limited to short sentences and brief status messages.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control is shown for the identity code (noted as console-only); password field is standard but long secrets are not presented with copy support.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry appears on any screen.

9.why: Standard email and password inputs with placeholders are present, which support browser autofill and password managers; code field is a normal text input.

10.why: Progress bar, clear headings, and prominent blue primary buttons make the current step and main action stand out on every screen.

11.why: Each screen presents one primary action (Sign in, Get identity code, Check code) with secondary options clearly de-emphasized.

12.why: Green status banners explicitly state what happened and what is next after each action, e.g. 'Signed in successfully. Next: get your identity code.'

13.why: A 'Re-request identity code' button is always available and the user can retry entry freely with no penalty indicated.

14.why: The error message states the problem and fix without blame: 'That code does not match. Check the six digits, or request a new code.'

15.why: An explicit banner states 'There is no reading timer. Take as long as you need.' and no timers appear on any screen.
